stories.title: H. pylori in children not clearly linked to asthma; IBD findings mixed
stories.summary: This review of 35 paediatric studies (7 on IBD) looked at H. pylori infection and allergic or immune conditions. In the asthma meta-analysis there was no significant overall association (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.54-1.05). Results for IBD and celiac disease were mixed and inconsistent.
stories.whyItMatters: It suggests there is no solid evidence yet that childhood H. pylori infection protects against or raises the risk of IBD.
stories.originalTitle: Paediatric Helicobacter pylori infection and allergic and inflammatory diseases: a contemporary systematic review with meta-analysis

stories.title: PRV-300 anti-TLR3 antibody safe enough but did not help ulcerative colitis
stories.summary: In a phase 1B trial, 38 people with moderate-to-severe UC were randomized (28 to PRV-300, 9 to placebo). Adverse events were more frequent with PRV-300 (50.0% vs 11.1%; serious events 39.3% vs 0.0%), but only 2 of 28 stopped treatment because of them. There were no differences in Mayo score or endoscopic severity.
stories.whyItMatters: This experimental drug is unlikely to become a UC treatment in its current form, and the result challenges TLR3 as a treatment target.
stories.originalTitle: Safety and tolerability of anti-toll-like receptor 3, monoclonal antibody PRV-300 in patients with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis: a randomized phase 1B clinical trial (PULSE)

stories.title: NGAL blood/stool marker may detect IBD but evidence is still too limited
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 78 studies compared NGAL with fecal calprotectin, CRP and ESR for diagnosing IBD. NGAL had pooled sensitivity of 90.9% and specificity of 76.1%, but estimates were very imprecise because only 4 studies had complete data. Authors concluded it should not replace fecal calprotectin or be used alone.
stories.whyItMatters: NGAL is an early-stage possible test, but established markers like fecal calprotectin remain the standard for now.
stories.originalTitle: Diagnostic accuracy of Neutrophil Gelatinase-Associated Lipocalin (NGAL) for inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review and bivariate diagnostic meta-analysis

stories.title: Switching children with IBD from IV to subcutaneous infliximab kept most in remission
stories.summary: A meta-analysis pooled six small pediatric cohorts (173 children) that switched from intravenous to subcutaneous infliximab. About 92% stayed on treatment and 93% stayed in clinical remission, while 8% stopped for any reason, mostly due to injection-site problems, relapse, or paradoxical dermatitis. New anti-drug antibodies were rare (four children, none sustained), and drug levels were about 2-fold higher than before the switch.
stories.whyItMatters: It suggests that subcutaneous infliximab, which is not yet approved for people under 18, may be a workable option that cuts school absence and travel for children with IBD, though the evidence comes from observational cohorts and still needs prospective confirmation.
stories.originalTitle: Switching from Intravenous to Subcutaneous Infliximab in Children with Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

stories.title: Tofacitinib 20 mg and 30 mg worked similarly in acute severe ulcerative colitis
stories.summary: In a small double-blind pilot trial of 72 adults with acute severe UC, all received IV corticosteroids plus tofacitinib at 20 or 30 mg/day. Clinical response at day 7 was 91.7% with 20 mg and 86.1% with 30 mg, a difference that was not statistically significant. Rescue therapy, treatment escalation or colectomy within 90 days was similar (event-free survival 83.3% vs 80.2%), and adverse events were mostly mild with no blood clots or major cardiovascular events reported.
stories.whyItMatters: This early evidence suggests that a higher tofacitinib dose may not add benefit over the lower dose in hospitalized severe UC, though the trial was too small to be conclusive.
stories.originalTitle: Tofacitinib 20 vs 30 mg in acute severe ulcerative colitis: a double-blind randomized controlled trial

stories.title: Machine learning shows promise for predicting anti-TNF response in Crohn's, especially with imaging data
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 29 studies with 6,697 Crohn's patients assessed machine learning models that predict response to anti-TNF therapy. In external validation, models using radiomic (imaging) features scored a C-index of 0.865, and models combining clinical and radiomic features scored 0.883. Models using clinical features alone scored 0.733. The authors noted methodological limitations.
stories.whyItMatters: In the future, such tools might help identify early who is unlikely to respond to anti-TNF drugs, but they need more validation across diverse groups of patients before routine use.
stories.originalTitle: The predictive value of machine learning for the response to anti-TNF-α therapy in patients with Crohn's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis

stories.title: Oral icotrokinra pill beat placebo for response in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis
stories.summary: In a phase 2b randomized trial of 252 adults with moderately to severely active UC, clinical response at week 12 was 63%, 58% and 55% with 400, 200 and 100 mg daily icotrokinra, versus 27% with placebo. At 400 mg, clinical remission was 30% vs 11% and endoscopic improvement was 37% vs 14%. Adverse events were similar across groups through week 28 (60-66%).
stories.whyItMatters: It suggests a once-daily pill that blocks the interleukin-23 pathway could one day be an alternative to injected or infused IL-23 antibodies, though larger and longer trials are needed.
stories.source: The New England journal of medicine
stories.originalTitle: Phase 2 Trial of Icotrokinra for Patients with Ulcerative Colitis

stories.title: Etrasimod lowers inflammatory immune cells in blood and gut lining in UC
stories.summary: Using blood from 782 and gut biopsies from 611 patients in the phase 3 ELEVATE UC trials, etrasimod reduced circulating T- and B-cell subsets at week 12 compared with placebo. Gut tissue showed fewer T cells, B cells, myeloid cells and neutrophils, with reduced IL-17 and IL-8 signaling. Changes consistent with tissue repair were most prominent in patients who reached remission.
stories.whyItMatters: It helps explain how this oral UC medication works on the immune system and the gut lining.
stories.originalTitle: Etrasimod reduces circulating and mucosal inflammatory lymphocyte populations and alters innate immune and non-immune cell signatures in intestinal mucosa: ELEVATE UC phase 3 clinical data

stories.title: Fast-recovery surgery pathways shorten hospital stays for people with IBD
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 18 studies (one randomized trial, 17 observational) found enhanced recovery protocols cut hospital stay by about 1.6 days (moderate certainty). There were no clear differences in 30-day readmissions, reoperations or complications, though certainty for these was low to very low.
stories.whyItMatters: If you need bowel surgery, enhanced recovery programs may mean a shorter hospital stay without evidence of more readmissions or complications, though the evidence is mostly observational.
stories.source: Colorectal disease : the official journal of the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland
stories.originalTitle: Enhanced recovery after colorectal surgery in patients with inflammatory bowel disease to reduce hospital length of stay: A systematic review and meta-analysis

stories.title: Stem cell therapy closed about 6 in 10 Crohn's perianal fistulas long-term
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 18 studies with 750 patients and 12 months to 4 years of follow-up found a pooled long-term healing rate of 59% in randomized trials and 63% across all designs. No treatment-related deaths or clear therapy-linked cancers were found.
stories.whyItMatters: It suggests stem cell treatment may give lasting healing for fistulas that haven't responded to standard care, although study designs differ.
stories.source: Colorectal disease : the official journal of the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland
stories.originalTitle: Long-term clinical outcomes of stem cell-based interventions in Crohn's-related perianal fistula: A systematic review and meta-analysis

stories.title: Under-the-skin infliximab kept most children with IBD in remission after switching
stories.summary: A pooled analysis of five cohorts (162 children, mostly Crohn's) found treatment persistence of about 90% and clinical remission of about 90% at roughly 6 months. Infliximab blood levels roughly doubled after the switch, new antidrug antibodies were rare (0.7%), and injection site reactions occurred in 11%. Certainty was low to very low, and nearly all children switched while already in remission.
stories.whyItMatters: It offers early reassurance for families considering a switch from intravenous to subcutaneous infliximab, which is currently off-label in children, but it does not show the injection can start treatment.
stories.originalTitle: Subcutaneous infliximab for maintenance therapy in children and adolescents with inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis

stories.title: Trial testing a phone-based CBT program for fatigue in IBD remission is under way
stories.summary: This is a protocol for an open-label, waitlist-controlled randomized trial of a 7-week app-based cognitive behavioral program for fatigue in people with IBD in remission. 351 patients were randomized; 151 of 502 screened were excluded for having little fatigue (FACIT-F of 40 or higher). No results are available yet and are expected in 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: Fatigue is common even in remission, and this trial could show whether a scalable app-based approach helps, but there are no findings yet.
stories.originalTitle: Evaluation of a Mental Health Care App-Based Fatigue Management Program for Patients With Inflammatory Bowel Disease in Remission: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial

stories.title: COVID-19 didn't worsen IBD course, but interrupted biologics raised flare risk
stories.summary: Across four matched cohorts (about 1,300 patients), prior COVID-19 was not linked to worse IBD course (OR 1.06; 95% CI 0.76-1.49). COVID-19 was linked to delayed or stopped biologics (OR 10.44), and flares were more frequent when biologics were delayed or stopped (about 52% vs 18%).
stories.whyItMatters: It suggests the bigger concern after COVID-19 may be interrupted IBD treatment rather than the infection itself, though the evidence is limited to a few observational cohorts.
stories.originalTitle: COVID-19 AND IBD: LOOK BEYOND THE VIRUS. A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS FOCUSED ON BIOLOGIC THERAPY CONTINUITY

stories.title: Neutrophil traps are high in IBD and blocking them eased colitis in animal models
stories.summary: A review of 48 studies found markers of neutrophil extracellular traps were raised in the gut and blood of people with IBD and linked to more severe disease and poorer prognosis. In animal models, blocking or breaking down these traps reduced disease activity and tissue damage and improved gut barrier function. Several results were not robust in sensitivity analyses.
stories.whyItMatters: This is early-stage science pointing to a possible future treatment target, with no human treatment trials yet.
stories.originalTitle: Neutrophil extracellular traps as a potential therapeutic target in inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis

stories.title: Stem cells and anti-TNF drugs both help Crohn's fistulas; no clear winner
stories.summary: A network meta-analysis of 15 randomized trials (2,475 patients) found stem cells improved fistula remission (OR 5.33) and response (OR 4.76) versus placebo. Anti-TNF drugs also improved fistula remission (OR 2.19) and were better for overall clinical remission (OR 2.41). Indirect comparison showed a non-significant trend favoring stem cells for fistula healing, and both had safety similar to placebo.
stories.whyItMatters: Both options appear to work for perianal Crohn's fistulas, but without head-to-head trials it is unclear which is better.
stories.originalTitle: Efficacy and safety of tumor necrosis factor-α inhibitors and mesenchymal stem cells in the treatment of fistulizing Crohn's disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis

stories.title: Balloon dilation of Crohn's strictures helped avoid surgery over 7 years better than stents
stories.summary: In a long-term follow-up of 80 patients from the ProtDilat trial (median 77 months), 31.5% needed surgery. Balloon dilatation (HR 0.26), a single endoscopic treatment (HR 0.33) and no medical therapy intensification (HR 0.22) were linked to lower surgery risk. Adverse events were less frequent with endoscopic treatment than surgery (8.75% vs 36%).
stories.whyItMatters: It suggests endoscopic balloon dilation can delay or avoid surgery for many people with Crohn's strictures, though this is a retrospective follow-up of an open-label trial.
stories.originalTitle: Self-expandable metal stents versus endoscopic balloon dilatation for the treatment of strictures in Crohn's disease: a retrospective long-term follow-up of the ProtDilat study, an open label, multicenter, randomized trial

stories.title: Mexico: COFEPRIS flags counterfeit Simponi (golimumab) syringes, an anti-TNF used in ulcerative colitis
stories.summary: On 5 October 2026 COFEPRIS issued an alert on fake Simponi (golimumab) 50 mg/0.5 mL pre-filled syringes, lot 01H201KE, expiry MAY/28. The importer Janssen-Cilag told the regulator it has no record of making or releasing that lot, so the lot is treated as counterfeit. COFEPRIS says identity, purity and efficacy can't be guaranteed. The alert covers one lot, so it doesn't show how widespread fakes are.
stories.whyItMatters: If you inject golimumab, check the lot number on your syringe against the alert. Buy only from licensed pharmacies or your hospital, and tell your care team if you got a pen or syringe from an informal source, such as a social-media seller or a friend.

stories.title: European biosimilar study: demand-side policies beat price cuts for uptake
stories.summary: A new analysis in The Lancet Regional Health – Europe (reported by a science news site) looked at which national policies actually raise biosimilar use. It found that lower prices alone do not reliably change prescribing. Doctors' reluctance to switch stable patients, over immunogenicity and equivalence, and patients' own safety fears were the main barriers. Hungary's price-link policy cut prices without raising uptake. The report is not specific to IBD, but it covers the anti-TNF class many people with Crohn's or UC use.
stories.whyItMatters: If your clinic proposes a non-medical switch to a biosimilar, ask how it will be monitored, such as drug levels and symptom checks, and who to call if you flare. Reassurance and clear information from the team appear to matter as much as the price.
stories.source: The Lancet Regional Health – Europe (via Bioengineer.org)

stories.title: Germany: pharmacies can now swap biologics for biosimilars, and big tenders were scrapped
stories.summary: Since 1 April 2026, German pharmacists may substitute a prescribed biologic with a cheaper biosimilar when strength, pack size, form, container and at least one indication and route match. The prescriber can rule out substitution for an individual patient. Just weeks later, lawmakers moved to ban exclusive biosimilar tenders for two years, which scrapped a joint insurer procurement worth about EUR 1.56 billion a year across 40 health funds. These are general biologic rules, not IBD-only, but they affect anti-TNF users.
stories.whyItMatters: If you live in Germany, ask your gastroenterologist whether you want substitution ruled out for your prescription, and check at the pharmacy that your pen or syringe is unchanged. Tell your team after any switch, so a flare can be linked to it quickly.
stories.source: Pharmaboardroom (industry interviews); rules also described by pharmazie.com

stories.title: Low muscle mass may signal tougher Crohn's disease and weaker biologic response, but the evidence is thin
stories.summary: A systematic review from Austria looked at sarcopenia (muscle loss) in IBD. It found 3 studies on endoscopic outcomes and 5 on biologic outcomes, mostly in Crohn's. Several linked low muscle to worse endoscopic results, post-surgery recurrence, loss of biologic response or shorter time on treatment. The authors say the studies were observational, varied and small, so the findings are hypothesis-generating only.
stories.whyItMatters: If you lift to build muscle, ask your IBD team whether your strength or body composition has been checked, and whether a dietitian should review your protein intake. Muscle loss is one more reason to treat training as part of care, though it does not yet change treatment decisions.
stories.source: Inflammatory Bowel Diseases (Crohn's & Colitis Foundation journals)

stories.title: NHANES analysis: adults with treated IBD show faster muscle-strength decline and lower lean mass
stories.summary: A US population-survey (NHANES) study in the Journal of Lifestyle Medicine reports accelerated loss of muscle strength and reduced lean mass in adults with treated IBD. The snippet I could access did not include effect sizes. The authors point to physical activity, resistance training and better nutrition as modifiable ways to protect muscle. As a cross-sectional survey, it cannot show cause and effect.
stories.whyItMatters: Strength loss can arrive earlier than you expect even when you are on treatment, so a gym habit is worth protecting. Ask your care team about grip-strength or lean-mass checks and about a resistance-training plan that fits your disease activity.
stories.date: 2026 (exact month not shown in the searc

stories.title: How serious-infection risk compares across advanced IBD drugs
stories.summary: AGA's GI & Hepatology News summarised a comparison of serious-infection risk across advanced IBD therapies. Compared with anti-TNF drugs, ustekinumab had an adjusted hazard ratio of 0.81 (95% CI 0.76–0.86), which means lower risk. JAK inhibitors had 1.27 (95% CI 1.12–1.43), which means higher risk. Another real-world UC study in January 2026 found JAK inhibitors had about 4-fold more adverse events than vedolizumab or ustekinumab. These are observational data, so the groups may differ in ways the analysis cannot fully correct for.
stories.whyItMatters: A late night out with a cold, or sharing drinks and vapes, matters more if your drug raises infection risk. Ask your care team which infections to watch for, what to do about fever, and whether your vaccines are up to date.

stories.title: Australian survey: most people with a stoma get little exercise advice, and those with a hernia get even less
stories.summary: A cross-sectional survey of Australians living with a stoma found that most were not getting evidence-based advice on returning to everyday activity and exercise. People with a parastomal hernia were about 3 times less likely to have been advised on core abdominal exercises. They were about 5 times less likely to have had those exercises demonstrated. The survey covered stoma patients in general, not only IBD.
stories.whyItMatters: If you have an ileostomy or colostomy, ask your stoma nurse or physio for a written plan for core work, lifting limits and when to use a support belt. Don't wait for them to bring it up.
stories.source: PMC-indexed cross-sectional survey (Australian stoma exercise study)

stories.title: Painkillers for gym aches: prescription NSAIDs looked acceptable in UC but not in Crohn's
stories.summary: A US claims-database study of more than 348,000 people compared IBD hospitalisations in people using prescription NSAIDs with matched controls. In UC, the hazard ratio for hospitalisation was 0.97, which met the non-inferiority margin of 1.2. In Crohn's disease, the NSAID group failed to meet that margin, so a higher risk could not be ruled out. This is a retrospective study, and the details here come from a summary page, not the full paper.
stories.whyItMatters: Before taking ibuprofen or similar painkillers for training soreness or a hangover, ask your gastroenterologist whether they are acceptable for your type of IBD. Ask too about alternatives for joint and muscle pain.
stories.source: Omnicuris MedShots summary of a retrospective claims study

stories.title: New IBD drug review: a broader mechanism did not translate into better results for etrolizumab in Crohn's
stories.summary: A review in Frontiers in Pharmacology says <cite index="21-1">the number of distinct advanced therapies has grown from one to more than a dozen, with regulators approving two S1P receptor modulators and a second JAK inhibitor between 2021 and 2026</cite>. It also recounts a setback. <cite index="21-1,21-2">Etrolizumab showed efficacy signals in Crohn's disease in BERGAMOT, but they did not support continuing, and IBD development was discontinued</cite>. The authors say <cite index="21-3">the episode is a caution against assuming a broader mechanism will bring greater efficacy</cite>.
stories.whyItMatters: A newer or broader-acting drug is not automatically a better one. Ask your care team why a particular advanced therapy suits you and what the plan is if it stops working.

stories.title: Mexico's COFEPRIS flags counterfeit Saizen growth hormone, a product that also circulates in gym culture
stories.summary: On 28 September 2026 COFEPRIS issued four alerts, one for falsified Saizen (somatropina, human growth hormone). A 1 October follow-up named five affected lots, and state health authorities said three fake lots lacked sterility conditions. Nothing in the alerts is specific to IBD, and they don't say who was buying the product. They matter for gym-goers because injectable products bought outside the legitimate supply chain carry unknown contents and handling.
stories.whyItMatters: If you take immune-suppressing IBD drugs, an infection from a non-sterile injectable is a bigger worry. Tell your IBD team about any injectable or performance product you use, and get medicines only through licensed pharmacies. You can report adverse reactions to COFEPRIS through VigiRam.

stories.title: Cannabis edibles plus alcohol impair driving more than either alone, and roadside tests often miss it
stories.summary: In a crossover trial in JAMA Network Open, <cite index="30-1">25 adults who took edibles and alcohol together showed greater driving impairment and subjective intoxication than with either substance alone</cite>. <cite index="30-2">Impairment from cannabis plus alcohol at 0.05% breath alcohol matched or exceeded alcohol alone at 0.08%</cite>. <cite index="31-2">Standard field sobriety tests often failed to detect cannabis impairment</cite>. The participants were healthy adults, not people with IBD, so this shows the general interaction risk and nothing about gut disease.
stories.whyItMatters: If you use cannabis for IBD symptoms and also drink on a night out, the combination is riskier than either alone. Plan a safe ride home, and ask your care team how alcohol interacts with your IBD medicines.

stories.title: Light at night and IBD: two large studies point in opposite directions
stories.summary: A Canadian population study in Inflammatory Bowel Diseases linked high outdoor night-time light to lower IBD risk and fewer IBD clinic visits and admissions. It found no link between light exposure at birth and later IBD among 3.93 million people, of whom 5,539 (0.1%) developed IBD. A UK Biobank cohort of 346,163 people followed for about 13.7 years found the reverse for ulcerative colitis. Higher outdoor light was tied to an 8% higher UC risk (HR 1.084), but not to Crohn's. Both studies are observational and measure street light, not your own late nights or screen use.
stories.whyItMatters: No one can say yet that late nights or city light cause IBD or flares, so this is not a reason to panic. If sleep is often broken, mention it to your IBD nurse or gastroenterologist, because sleep can be tracked alongside symptoms.
stories.source: Gastroenterology Advisor (reporting Inflammatory Bowel Diseases; UK Biobank cohort in Frontiers in Public Health)

stories.title: Brazil's GEDIIB publishes its first IBD nutrition consensus, covering exclusion diets and supplements
stories.summary: 22 specialists (11 dietitians, 8 gastroenterologists, 3 colorectal surgeons) wrote the consensus, published in Arquivos de Gastroenterologia on 10 August 2026. They built it on a systematic review, and a modified Delphi panel endorsed every statement with at least 80% agreement. It covers nutritional screening, diet in active disease and remission, exclusion diets and supplementation. The abstracts I found don't give gym-specific advice, such as on protein shakes or sports supplements.
stories.whyItMatters: If you train and use shakes, powders or other supplements, take the product labels to a dietitian who knows IBD. Ask whether they fit your disease activity and any exclusion diet you follow.

stories.title: Trimbos: a lifetime of heavy drinking tied to 25% more colorectal cancer (general population, not IBD)
stories.summary: The Trimbos Institute summarised a US study of 88,092 adults aged 55–74. Those averaging 14 or more drinks a week over their lives had 25% higher colorectal cancer risk than those drinking one or fewer. Their rectal cancer risk was 95% higher. Ex-drinkers had a 42% lower risk of an early polyp than people who still drank. A Belgian fact-check says the study shows no increase for light-to-moderate drinkers. The study did not look at people with IBD, who already need regular colonoscopies.
stories.whyItMatters: The risk here is cumulative heavy drinking, not an occasional night out, but IBD adds its own bowel-cancer surveillance needs. Ask your care team how often your colonoscopy is due, and be honest with them about how much you drink.
stories.source: Trimbos-instituut (Expertisecentrum Alcohol); fact-check by Gezondheid en Wetenschap

stories.title: STRIDE-III published: updated international treat-to-target goals for IBD
stories.summary: The International Organization for the Study of IBD published STRIDE-III in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology. It separates targets that should prompt a change in treatment from those that mainly guide optimisation and monitoring. It also adds a separate patient-centred pathway based on shared decision-making. This is an expert consensus framework, not a trial.
stories.whyItMatters: It may shape how clinicians set and review goals such as symptoms, endoscopy and biomarkers. It also formally includes patient preferences in setting targets.

stories.title: Mirikizumab in Crohn's: about 1 in 5 reached steroid-free deep remission at one year, linked to better quality of life
stories.summary: A post hoc analysis of the phase 3 VIVID-1 trial was presented at UEG Week 2026 in Barcelona. About 1 in 5 people with moderate-to-severe Crohn's on mirikizumab (Omvoh) reached corticosteroid-free deep remission at 1 year. Deep remission combines clinical and endoscopic remission. It was tied to remission on the IBDQ quality-of-life measure. Because the analysis was post hoc, it cannot prove cause and effect.
stories.whyItMatters: It suggests that reaching a stricter combined target is accompanied by better day-to-day wellbeing, not just better scope findings. About 4 in 5 people did not reach that target, though.
stories.source: HCPLive reporting on a UEG Week 2026 presentation

stories.title: China's regulator fast-tracks local manufacturing of etrasimod (Velsipity) for ulcerative colitis
stories.summary: China's drug regulator (NMPA) approved the once-daily oral drug etrasimod for moderate-to-severe UC in February 2026. In October 2026, its Center for Drug Evaluation accepted Everest Medicines' application to make the drug locally, with priority review. Everest expects local production to start in 2027, subject to approval.
stories.whyItMatters: Local manufacturing may improve supply of a newly approved oral UC option in China, though timing and pricing are not yet known. This is a company-reported milestone, not new efficacy data.

stories.title: Dutch adult IBD guideline: drug-treatment modules for UC and Crohn's updated
stories.summary: The Dutch national guideline 'Inflammatoire darmziekten volwassenen' was republished on 3 September 2026. Updated modules include drug treatment of ulcerative colitis and of Crohn's disease, biologicals and JAK inhibitors in each condition, and the surveillance modality. The summary page lists which modules changed but gives no recommendation details, so check the full modules for the actual advice.
stories.whyItMatters: Dutch gastroenterologists use this guideline to choose between biologicals and JAK inhibitors and to plan colonoscopy surveillance. People in the Netherlands can ask their IBD team what has changed for them.

stories.title: Meta-analysis: surgical recurrence after first ileocolic resection for Crohn's ileitis has fallen about 3-fold in the biologics era
stories.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis in Inflammatory Bowel Diseases found that 5- and 10-year surgical recurrence after a first ileocolic resection for Crohn's ileitis fell to 5.7% and 13.0% in the biologics era (post-2000). The analysis also looked at predictors of repeat surgery.
stories.whyItMatters: It gives realistic, contemporary figures on how often repeat surgery is needed after a first bowel resection. These are pooled averages, not predictions for any one person.
stories.source: Inflammatory Bowel Diseases (Oxford University Press / Crohn's & Colitis Foundation)

stories.title: Review update on diet and nutrition therapies in IBD covers ultra-processed food, Mediterranean diet and food insecurity
stories.summary: A June 2026 open-access review in Digestive Diseases and Sciences summarizes dietary evidence in IBD. It notes that large cohorts link higher ultra-processed food intake to more Crohn's disease, while a Mediterranean-style diet is linked to lower IBD risk. It also flags food insecurity as a practical barrier: one survey found 19% of patients worried food would run out.
stories.whyItMatters: The review gathers diet findings in one place and treats cost and food access as part of nutrition care. Most of the cohort links are associations and do not prove that changing diet alters IBD.

stories.title: Setback: J&J's guselkumab + golimumab combination (DUET) misses its primary endpoint in phase 2b
stories.summary: Johnson & Johnson's DUET phase 2b trials tested combining Tremfya (guselkumab) and Simponi (golimumab) in UC and Crohn's. STAT reported that the combination did better than either drug alone but did not meet the primary endpoint of clinical remission in either trial. NBC reported a 49.2% clinical remission rate at 48 weeks in the high-dose, most treatment-resistant Crohn's group, versus 27.3% for guselkumab alone and 23.1% for golimumab alone. Safety was similar.
stories.whyItMatters: Combining two advanced drugs is being studied for people who have not responded to several treatments. This result shows it is not yet an established option, and it is not available outside trials. Gains in resistant subgroups may guide future studies.

stories.title: Calgary RCT: eating within an 8-hour window cut Crohn's disease activity by about 40%
stories.summary: In a 12-week randomized trial of 35 adults with Crohn's disease and overweight or obesity, time-restricted feeding (8-hour eating window, 16 hours fasting) cut symptomatic disease activity by 40% and abdominal discomfort by 50% versus usual eating. Participants lost weight and had better inflammation and immune markers. This happened even though they did not cut calories or change what they ate. The trial was funded by the Crohn's & Colitis Foundation and led by the University of Calgary.
stories.whyItMatters: Meal timing could become a low-cost add-on to care for people with Crohn's and excess weight. The trial was small and short, and it enrolled only people with overweight or obesity, so it does not show long-term effects or apply to everyone with Crohn's.

stories.title: VERDICT: aiming for 'disease clearance' rather than symptom control alone cut UC complications by about 70% with vedolizumab
stories.summary: This is the first randomized treat-to-target trial in UC. It compared steroid-free disease clearance with steroid-free symptomatic remission in people on intravenous vedolizumab. Disease clearance lengthened the time to a first UC-related complication (hazard ratio 0.33, 95% CI 0.17–0.67). Results were presented at UEG Week and published in United European Gastroenterology Journal. The trial was sponsored by Takeda, and the figures come from its press release.
stories.whyItMatters: It supports the idea that checking the gut lining and not only symptoms may lead to fewer complications. Treatment targets are decided with your care team, and this study does not change that.
stories.source: Takeda press release (UEG Week 2026; UEG Journal)

stories.title: Guselkumab (Tremfya) keeps perianal fistula remission going through 48 weeks in Crohn's: FUZION phase 3
stories.summary: Johnson & Johnson reported one-year results from the phase 3 FUZION study in adults with Crohn's disease and perianal fistula. Guselkumab maintained or improved fistula remission through week 48, building on the earlier week-24 results. The data were a late-breaker at UEG Week 2026. This is a company release, and the snippet I found gave no detailed numbers.
stories.whyItMatters: Perianal fistulas are among the hardest Crohn's complications to treat. Durable healing data may help people and clinicians weigh long-term options. The release is company-reported and has not yet been peer-reviewed.
stories.source: Johnson & Johnson press release (UEG Week 2026 late-breaker)

stories.title: Gilead's oral emvistegrast beats placebo in phase 2 SWIFT ulcerative colitis trial
stories.summary: At the 200 mg dose, 66% of patients had a clinical response versus 37% on placebo. Clinical remission was 31% versus 8%. Adverse events were reported in 36% of participants and the drug was described as generally well tolerated. Gilead plans late-stage trials in 2027. These are company-reported, 12-week phase 2 results.
stories.whyItMatters: It adds another once-daily oral candidate to the UC pipeline. It is still years from any approval, and longer-term safety is unknown.
stories.source: Benzinga / GuruFocus reporting Gilead's UEG Week late-breaker

stories.title: Obefazimod (oral, first-in-class) clears FDA pre-NDA meeting after phase 3 ABTECT UC maintenance results
stories.summary: Abivax's once-daily oral obefazimod reached the primary endpoint in the phase 3 ABTECT maintenance trial in ulcerative colitis. Clinical remission at week 44 was about 51% on drug, against 10.4% on placebo, and both doses had p<0.0001. The company has completed a pre-NDA interaction with the FDA. A later company release reported that 37.2% of induction non-responders reached clinical remission at week 44 on continued 50 mg. The company's own materials say the NDA is planned for later this year.
stories.whyItMatters: If approved, it would add a new oral mechanism for UC. Safety, including the skin cancer and malignancy rates the company says are within background rates, will be reviewed by regulators. Nothing is approved yet.

stories.title: Cell therapy AVB-114 for stubborn Crohn's perianal fistulas: STOMP2 results summarised after ECCO 2026
stories.summary: In the wait-list controlled phase 2 STOMP2 trial, combined remission at 9 months was 45.8% (11 of 24) with AVB-114 and 8.3% (2 of 24) with standard care. In the wait-list arm, 44.4% (4 of 9) reached clinical remission after later receiving AVB-114. Two serious events were reported, and only one (proctalgia) was attributed to the treatment. Most adverse events were mild post-operative perianal pain.
stories.whyItMatters: Complex perianal fistulas often fail biologics and surgery. A cell-seeded plug that closes fistulas in a good share of patients could add an option, though the trial was small and the therapy is not yet approved.

stories.title: Meta-analysis from India: Crohn's disease exclusion diet gets about 69% clinical remission in pooled data
stories.summary: Researchers at PGIMER Chandigarh pooled 17 studies (16 with quantitative data) of the Crohn's disease exclusion diet (CDED). Pooled clinical remission at 6–8 weeks was 0.69 (95% CI 0.65–0.74). Odds of remission were higher than with a control diet (OR 2.58) and than with exclusive enteral nutrition (OR 2.05). The pooled maintenance-of-remission rate was 0.64, but results varied widely between studies (I²=73.5%).
stories.whyItMatters: This pools the evidence behind a food-based option that may be easier to tolerate than liquid-only feeding. The high variability in maintenance results and the small, mixed studies mean it is not proof that the diet suits everyone.

stories.title: Health Canada crackdown on illegal injectable peptides, steroids and SARMs sold as bodybuilding products
stories.summary: A secondary research write-up from 16 October 2026 reviews Health Canada enforcement against sellers of unauthorized bodybuilding products. It says Health Canada reported seizures at two supplement stores in Maple Ridge, BC. The seized items included injectable peptides, steroids and SARMs, and some carried falsified Drug Identification Numbers. The write-up also says Health Canada is working with border services to stop unauthorized shipments, and that online purchases may be refused entry or seized. The source is a trade-oriented site rather than Health Canada itself. I did not find the original Health Canada notice or confirm the seizure dates.
stories.whyItMatters: A hard gainer looking for a shortcut should avoid 'research peptides', SARMs and steroid-labelled products. They are unauthorized, can be mislabelled or counterfeit, and aren't approved for adding muscle. Health Canada's bodybuilding-products page is the place to check.
stories.source: Blue Nex Labs (summarizing Health Canada enforcement records)

stories.title: Large meta-analysis puts a number on lean-mass gain from about 10 weeks of lifting: roughly 1.5 kg on average, with huge individual spread
stories.summary: A McMaster University analysis of 111 resistance-training studies (951 men) found an average fat-free mass gain of about 1.53 kg after roughly 10 weeks, or about 150 g per week. The range was wide: the lowest gainers added only 0.44 kg, the highest more than 3 kg, and one outlier gained 5.6 kg. The page is a Dutch men's-magazine summary of the review, and its exact date is not shown in the text I found, only that it is about 100 days old.
stories.region: Netherlands (Dutch-language coverage of a Canadian study)
stories.whyItMatters: Hard gainers should expect slow progress. Judge it over a full 10–12 week block rather than week to week, and know that low responders are common. Keep training and eating consistently instead of chasing extreme programs.
stories.source: Men's Health NL (summarising McMaster University meta-analysis)

stories.title: One long leg day vs three short sessions: more work done, but no clear extra muscle in trained men
stories.summary: In a six-week study of 18 men with lifting experience, lower-body training was either done in one session or split over three. The split group did considerably more total training work. That did not translate into demonstrably more muscle growth or strength. The page is a Dutch fitness-press write-up of the study, and I could not confirm the exact day it was published.
stories.region: Netherlands (Dutch-language coverage of an international stu
stories.whyItMatters: If you struggle to recover or to fit in sessions, splitting leg work over three days is not needed for growth. Pick whatever schedule you can keep up while still eating enough to grow.

stories.title: Crohn's patients on infliximab: half had weak grip strength even though none met full sarcopenia criteria
stories.summary: In 84 adults with Crohn's disease on infliximab, half had muscle strength below age- and sex-adjusted norms (probable sarcopenia). None met full sarcopenia criteria because none had low muscle mass, and one third had slow gait speed. Ileocolonic disease and lower hemoglobin predicted low strength.
stories.whyItMatters: If you have Crohn's, normal muscle size does not guarantee normal strength. Ask for grip-strength or gait testing, and check for anemia, instead of relying on body composition alone.

stories.title: Large prospective cohort: people with sarcopenia had a higher later risk of developing IBD
stories.summary: A large prospective cohort study in Geriatrics & Gerontology International found that sarcopenic individuals had an increased risk of developing IBD. The authors call for targeted screening in high-risk groups and for interventions that improve physical capability. The abstract excerpt I found does not give effect sizes.
stories.whyItMatters: This is observational data, so it does not show that low muscle causes IBD. It does suggest that persistent unexplained weakness or low muscle is worth raising with a doctor, especially if you also have GI symptoms.

stories.title: Colombian IBD study (NUTRIBD-COL): malnutrition tracked with worse quality of life, and nutritional support helped
stories.summary: In Colombian IBD patients, malnutrition was significantly linked to worse quality of life, especially mobility, self-care and daily activities. Among hospitalised adults, 25% had sarcopenia, and Crohn's disease carried a much higher malnutrition risk (odds ratio about 25). In the paediatric group, nutritional support improved nutritional status in 75% of cases within three months.
stories.whyItMatters: Weight and muscle loss in IBD are not only a cosmetic issue. They affect daily function, and structured nutritional support can reverse them in many cases. Ask for a formal nutrition screen, especially with Crohn's or during hospital stays.

stories.title: Systematic review in trained lifters: training volume load is the variable most consistently tied to muscle growth
stories.summary: The review searched the literature up to April 2025 and assessed 52 full-text articles. It examined how different resistance-training variables relate to hypertrophy in resistance-trained people. Total volume load was the variable most consistently linked to muscle growth. The abstract excerpt I found did not give pooled effect sizes.
stories.whyItMatters: Progressively adding total work (sets × reps × load) is the most reliable lever for adding muscle. Fine-tuning other details is less important.
stories.source: Journal of Bodywork and Movement Therapies

stories.title: Pre-workout powder recalled in the US for undeclared DMAA, a stimulant linked to heart attack risk
stories.summary: A Texas company, Leader Formulas, recalled one lot of RAPTURE pre-workout powder on 6 October 2026 after testing found 1,3-dimethylamylamine (DMAA). The FDA gave the recall its highest risk level, Class I. The product was sold nationwide and online between January 2025 and May 2026. The company said it had received no reports of adverse events.
stories.whyItMatters: Hard gainers are often sold stimulant-heavy 'pre-workout' or appetite and energy products. Skip them. They add no calories or muscle, and DMAA raises blood pressure and cardiovascular risk.

stories.title: Meta-analysis: when weekly volume is equal, training a muscle 1, 2 or 3 times a week builds the same size
stories.summary: A preprint pooled 16 trials (380 participants) lasting at least 6 weeks that matched weekly sets between frequencies. It found a trivial, non-significant frequency effect (g = -0.02; 95% CI -0.21 to 0.16). The authors say the data allow at most a small edge for higher frequency. The preprint is not yet peer reviewed.
stories.whyItMatters: A hard gainer can split the same weekly sets across 1 to 3 sessions per muscle, whichever schedule is easiest to stick with. Total weekly volume matters more than how often you train each muscle.

stories.title: Bayesian network meta-analysis ranks protein types and doses combined with resistance training
stories.summary: The analysis by Korea-based authors compared protein supplement types, doses and populations alongside resistance training. For strength (1-RM), whey ranked highest (SUCRA 0.84), ahead of casein (0.71) and milk protein (0.63). The whey-versus-placebo difference was +5.8 kg (95% credible interval 1.9 to 9.7).
stories.whyItMatters: If you use a protein powder to reach your daily target, whey is the best-supported choice for strength gains with lifting. The result is a ranking of products, not proof that powders beat whole-food protein.

stories.title: IBD-FITT: 12 weeks of moderate exercise did not significantly improve quality of life in active IBD (null result)
stories.summary: This Danish open-label RCT in J Clin Med (March 2026) screened 183 patients with active IBD and randomised 44, 22 per arm. Quality of life on the IBDQ did not differ significantly between groups (predicted scores 172 vs 164 at week 12). Only 11 participants completed more than half of the exercise sessions. Secondary outcomes included BMI and waist circumference, not muscle mass.
stories.whyItMatters: Supervised aerobic exercise during a flare did not clearly help quality of life, and half the participants struggled to attend. The trial did not test resistance training or muscle gain, so it does not settle whether lifting helps underweight IBD patients.

stories.title: TGA warns that Eagle Research Lab SARMs are significantly underdosed and unsafe
stories.summary: TGA laboratory testing of Eagle Research Lab SR-9009, S-23, YK-11 and RAD-140 found far less active ingredient than the label states. The regulator says these products pose a serious health risk and should not be taken. All SARMs are prescription-only medicines in Australia.
stories.whyItMatters: Shortcuts for 'hard gainers' such as online SARMs are unapproved, mislabelled and potentially harmful. Even the dose you think you are taking can't be trusted. Food, training and creatine are the safer route.

stories.title: Dutch guideline on malnutrition and sarcopenia in frail older adults updated with treatment chapters
stories.summary: The Dutch guideline database published new treatment sections for malnutrition and sarcopenia on 1 September 2026. Screening and measurement chapters were updated in January 2026. The guideline uses the GLIM approach. Malnutrition is diagnosed when at least one body criterion is present (low BMI, unintended weight loss or low muscle mass) together with one cause (low intake or disease burden/inflammation). Sarcopenia follows the EWGSOP2 steps of strength, then muscle mass, then physical function. The pages I could access did not show the treatment recommendations themselves.
stories.whyItMatters: The diagnostic criteria are the same ones Dutch dietitians and doctors use for underweight patients, including those with IBD. Knowing them helps you ask for a muscle-mass and strength check, not only a BMI check. The guideline targets frail older adults, so it does not directly apply to younger hard gainers.

stories.title: Preprint: fixed 2–3 minute rests matched self-selected rests for lower-body muscle gain and saved about 22 minutes per session
stories.summary: In an 8-week study of trained adults (Mohan et al., 2026), fixed rests of about 2.4 minutes gave similar lower-body muscle thickness, strength and endurance results to self-selected rests of about 3.7 minutes. Fixed-rest workouts averaged 56 minutes, versus 78.5 minutes with self-selected rest. This is a SportRxiv preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and I read it through a secondary summary.
stories.whyItMatters: Resting a fixed 2–3 minutes between sets is enough for lower-body growth. Waiting until you feel fully recovered adds time without extra muscle.
stories.source: Evidence Based Muscle (summarizing a SportRxiv preprint)
